presentation.label: VEL HUMANISE
presentation.summary: Per track, every trig's velocity gets a random offset of up to ±N, set with FUNC + VEL on the TRIG page.
presentation.overview: Velocity Humanise gives each track a random velocity offset: every trig's velocity moves by a random amount up to ±N, clamped to 1..127. N is one of sixteen steps from 0 to 64, set by holding FUNC and turning VEL on the TRIG page, where the label reads RND and the knob becomes a sixteen-position selector. N is per pattern track, kept in core-ar2's mod storage and saved with the pattern. It is an elemod port of MrScruff's rytm-mods 0003-velocity-humanise, with his code unchanged apart from the storage port.
highlights: FUNC + VEL sets a per-track random velocity range.
Sixteen steps from 0 to 64; 0 is stock behaviour.
Kept in core-ar2 mod storage and saved with the pattern.
No longer needs Euclid Accents in the same build.
usage: Use a build containing Velocity Humanise. On the TRIG page, hold FUNC and turn VEL: the label reads RND and the popup shows N.
Set N to 32 and play a track of equal-velocity trigs: the hits vary in level. Set N to 0: they are equal again.
Release FUNC: VEL is the trig velocity again, unchanged.

access.location: TRIG page: the VEL knob with FUNC held.
steps: Hold FUNC and turn VEL to set N.

controls.name: FUNC + VEL (TRIG page)
controls.doc: Sets the track's random velocity range N: sixteen steps from 0 to 64. Each trig's velocity moves by a random amount up to ±N, clamped to 1..127.

limitations: Built for OS 1.74 only, with core-ar2 0.3.
Needs core-ar2 0.3's mod storage: four bits per pattern track (vel_rnd). Earlier cores lose N at a power-off without a project save.
On stock firmware, or a build without this module, the track plays its plain velocities: N is in mod storage, which stock ignores.
Patches param_apply_delta and param_value_text next to other gate-chain modules; each has its own site and they link together.

load.display: Small: a storage read, a random draw and a clamp on each trig
load.conditions: Static: one detour runs per trig in the sequencer; it reads the track's N through core_store_get, which masks interrupts briefly, then draws and clamps the offset. The others run on UI edits and drawing. Not a measurement.

hardware.summary: Iced-Cream reports that on an Analog Rytm MKII with OS 1.74, velocity-humanise 1.1 passed test steps 1 to 3 (FUNC + VEL reads RND, N = 32 varies the hits and N = 0 does not, N kept through save and power-cycle) with core-ar2 0.3 and all eleven rytm2_mods ports in C3A4, with N kept through a power-cycle without SAVE PROJECT, and step 4 (the same without euclid-accents) on C3N4 (2026-10-20). On SXH4 (released core-ar2 0.3 with the other five Modwerk 1.74 submissions, 2026-10-24/25) N 10 measurably varied CP's equal-velocity hits where N 0 did not, and N was kept through a power cycle without SAVE PROJECT. Alone on VHH4 (released core-ar2 0.3 and this module only, 2026-10-25) N 64 spread CP's equal-velocity hits by about 3 dB where N 0 did not.
limitations: Tested builds: C3A4, .syx 04d987ced36850eef5eb5cd1215d411edf621a5af94f980525ab561c9108f951; C3N4, .syx a74435c28591ec0f2d143b0629a4fd5b6f37ab85e0b3e4618b000698dd5ea9f5. Firmware was not read back from the device.

SXH4 (the released core-ar2 0.3, 2026-10-24/25, .syx e4d01a6aec250bd2af7743c9f8b0e9c560d805b52564932dddc41d872e1c5000) also carried a remote-control test layer that shares no site with core or the modules. VHH4 (alone with the released core-ar2 0.3, 2026-10-25, .syx 4bebbd5d7ba1860f168ee34c35212f58e67b525628a91b6f7d76fd5e5a101ca8) carried the same test layer.

tests.summary: Hardware: velocity-humanise 1.1's test steps pass on an Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74, with core-ar2 0.3 (C3A4 and, without euclid-accents, C3N4, 2026-10-20), and N survives a power-cycle without a project save. Modwerk's source build gives a main OS byte-identical to elekloader's build of the rytm2_mods v1.2 release. In rytm-emu, holding FUNC on the TRIG page relabels VEL as RND and turning it shows N, where stock changes VEL.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Use a build containing Velocity Humanise. On the TRIG page, hold FUNC and turn VEL: the label reads RND and the popup shows N.
Set N to 32 and play a track of equal-velocity trigs: the hits vary in level. Set N to 0: they are equal again.
Release FUNC: VEL is the trig velocity again, unchanged.
